subject: Private Terraform modules (alpha) — gate criteria + pilot timeline (sign-off + doc review)
body:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 13, 2025 at 9:12 AM PST
Subject: Private Terraform modules (alpha) — gate criteria + pilot timeline (sign-off + doc review)

Team —

We’re at the point where we need to lock the alpha gate criteria + confirm the pilot window, so we can stop thrashing and hold a single “this is alpha” line across Product/Infra/Sec.

I’m proposing the following as the alpha gate (draft checklist attached):

1) Reproducible deploy in a fresh AWS account using reference modules (default topology) with documented prerequisites.
2) CI gates passing in redwood-terraform:
   - terraform fmt/validate
   - tflint + checkov (with documented suppressions)
   - at least one integration plan/apply in ephemeral account
3) Security sign-off on “secure-by-default” posture (SG defaults, flow logs options, encryption hooks guidance).
4) Docs: overview + quickstart + troubleshooting + versioning/rollback notes published (internal Confluence at minimum; docs-site draft ok for alpha).
5) Pilot: at least one customer pilot completed with measured deployment time reduction (baseline vs modules) + support readiness.

Ask:
- Irene: confirm topology + supported patterns for alpha (and explicit non-supported combos), and whether we’re comfortable calling single NAT the default.
- Marcus/Kevin: confirm what security needs to see for sign-off + any exceptions we’re explicitly allowing for alpha.
- Talia: align on dates and reviewers (who signs what, and by when).

Links for review (current drafts):
- vpc-terraform-modules-alpha-overview (Confluence)
- aws-vpc-terraform-quickstart-alpha (Confluence)
- vpc-terraform-alpha-secure-defaults-review (Confluence)
- ADR-0127 + ADR-0128

If we can converge by EOD Tue (2/18), we can treat Wed (2/19) as “alpha gate met” internally and move to pilot execution.

Thanks,
Vivek
Product — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Alpha_Gate_Criteria_Private_Terraform_Modules_v0.3.pdf

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 13, 2025 at 11:04 AM PST
Subject: Re: Private Terraform modules (alpha) — gate criteria + pilot timeline (sign-off + doc review)

Agree with the gate list.

On topology/defaults:
- Default subnet tiers (3-tier): public (ALB/bastion optional), private (nodes), isolated (datastores/control plane components where applicable).
- Default NAT: single NAT to start for alpha.
  - Rationale: cost + fewer moving parts; our support burden is lower.
  - We should keep “per-AZ NAT” as an option with a strong note that it increases cost.
- Explicit non-supported for alpha (needs to be called out in docs + module validations where possible):
  - Changing CIDRs after create (we can document but not support).
  - “No NAT + no private endpoints + still expecting image pulls” (people keep attempting this).
  - Mixed ‘existing VPC’ mode + module-created route tables (too many unsafe combos).

I’ll add a short “supported patterns” section to the overview page and tag it as the canonical list.

One more: we should call STS out more prominently as required in private-only patterns. We’ve seen installs fail when STS isn’t reachable.

-Irene
Infra

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 14, 2025 at 8:37 AM PST
Subject: Re: Private Terraform modules (alpha) — gate criteria + pilot timeline (sign-off + doc review)

Thanks. This is close.

Security sign-off requirements for alpha (minimum):
1) SG defaults are least-privilege by component and deny-by-default (no 0.0.0.0/0 ingress). Any “escape hatch” variables must be clearly named, validated, and documented as customer-owned risk.
2) VPC Flow Logs: modules must support enabling flow logs with a default posture that doesn’t surprise customers (i.e., off by default is acceptable for alpha if we provide a recommended config + retention guidance).
3) Endpoint policies: ok to have “policy stubs” as long as docs state customers should tighten policies and we don’t claim restrictive defaults where we don’t enforce them.
4) DNS: private DNS toggles need explicit warnings. If a customer turns off private DNS, the installer should fail early with actionable messaging.

Exceptions we can accept for alpha:
- Not prescribing NACLs (we can provide guidance text, but don’t ship opinionated NACL resources yet).

Kevin can weigh in on logging/audit specifics, but from my side: if the secure defaults review page is updated to reflect the above and the SG module has input validation, I’m comfortable signing.

-Marcus
Security

From: Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 14, 2025 at 10:22 AM PST
Subject: Re: Private Terraform modules (alpha) — gate criteria + pilot timeline (sign-off + doc review)

+1 to Marcus’s list.

For flow logs guidance, please make sure the docs include:
- Destination options (CloudWatch vs S3) and the implications (IAM permissions + cost + retention).
- Suggested retention defaults (e.g., 30 days CW logs as baseline, longer retention in S3 if customer needs it).
- A sentence that Redwood doesn’t ingest customer flow logs by default; this is customer-controlled for audit/forensics.

Also: if we’re calling this “secure by default,” I want the quickstart to *explicitly* show the locked-down/private-only variant, not just the minimal happy path.

-Kevin
Security Engineering

From: Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 17, 2025 at 3:16 PM PST
Subject: Re: Private Terraform modules (alpha) — gate criteria + pilot timeline (sign-off + doc review)

Proposed dates + owners:

Gate review meeting: Wed 2/19 11:00–11:30am PT
- Attendees: Vivek, Irene, Marcus (Kevin optional), me
- Goal: confirm “alpha gate met” and greenlight pilot kickoff

By EOD Tue 2/18 (please comment in Confluence pages, not email, where possible):
- Infra sign-off: Irene (topology + supported patterns section + NAT default language)
- Security sign-off: Marcus (secure defaults review page) + Kevin (flow log/audit guidance)
- Product sign-off: Vivek (gate checklist + alpha messaging, pilot success metrics)

Pilot timeline (assuming gate passes):
- Thu 2/20: pilot kickoff call (PS + customer)
- Week of 2/24: install + validation
- Week of 3/03: feedback, close gaps, publish “known limitations” section

Open items I’m tracking:
- Ensure installer networking preflight checks match the docs (especially STS + ECR endpoints + private DNS assumptions).
- Confirm the exit metric definition for “deployment time reduction” (what’s the baseline?).

I’ll send calendar hold for 2/19.

-Talia
Program Management

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Tue, Feb 18, 2025 at 9:48 AM PST
Subject: Re: Private Terraform modules (alpha) — gate criteria + pilot timeline (sign-off + doc review)

Thanks — aligned.

Updates from my side:
- I updated the gate checklist with explicit alpha language (what we do/don’t support) and the pilot success metric proposal:
  - Measure: time from “repo cloned + AWS creds ready” to “installer passes networking preflight + pulls images successfully”
  - Compare: customer’s prior manual setup estimate vs module-driven setup (we’ll capture both)

Also adding to the gate:
- Docs must include a “Common failure modes” section with exact errors + fix steps (missing STS endpoint, ECR dkr/api endpoints, private DNS disabled, S3 gateway endpoint missing route).

Irene: please make sure the overview page has a prominent “STS required (private-only)” callout.
Marcus/Kevin: once you’ve commented in the secure defaults page, I’ll address and request final +1.

-Vivek

Subject: Re: Private Terraform modules (alpha) — gate criteria + pilot timeline (sign-off + doc review)

I left comments on the secure defaults review page (mostly wording + one validation request).

If the SG module validates against:
- accidental public ingress rules, and
- a “custom ingress” variable requiring explicit CIDR blocks (no implicit wide-open),

…then I’m good to approve for alpha.

Also +1 to the expanded failure-mode docs; that will reduce back-and-forth during pilot.

-Marcus
